name: Wintershall Dea

summary.text: Wintershall Dea was a German oil and gas producer owned 72.7 percent by BASF and 27.3 percent by LetterOne. It was one of five European companies that lent money to Gazprom's Nord Stream 2 pipeline; within days of Russia's February 2022 invasion of Ukraine it wrote off about 1 billion euros of those loans and halted payments to Russia, and in January 2023 it announced a full exit from Russia, booking a non-cash loss of about 5.3 billion euros from deconsolidating its Russian joint ventures. In December 2023 BASF and LetterOne agreed to sell Wintershall Dea's exploration and production business, excluding its Russia-related activities, to Harbour Energy at an enterprise value of $11.2 billion; the transaction closed on September 3, 2024.

facts.claim: Wintershall Dea was owned by BASF (72.7 percent) and LetterOne (27.3 percent) at the time of the sale of its exploration and production business to Harbour Energy.

facts.claim: In March 2022, within days of Russia's invasion of Ukraine, Wintershall Dea wrote off roughly 1 billion euros of loans it had made to finance Gazprom's Nord Stream 2 pipeline, said it would pursue no new projects in Russia and stopped payments to Russia; Gazprom was the pipeline's sole owner, with Wintershall Dea, OMV, Shell, Engie and Uniper providing loans.

Wintershall writes down Nord Stream 2 loans

facts.claim: Wintershall Dea's first-quarter 2022 results included a 1.5 billion euro impairment on Russia-related assets, producing a net loss of about 1 billion euros for the quarter.

sources.title: Wintershall Dea special media call and 1Q22 results

facts.claim: In January 2023 Wintershall Dea announced that it intended to exit Russia fully, its chief executive Mario Mehren saying that continuing to operate there was not tenable and describing Russian government limits on Western companies and interference in its joint ventures as an economic expropriation; it booked a non-cash loss of about 5.3 billion euros from deconsolidating its Russian joint ventures and impairing its interests in Nord Stream AG and WIGA Transport Beteiligungs.

sources.title: Nord Stream Partner to Withdraw from Russia
Wintershall Dea effects full Russia exit, records EUR 5.3bn impairment

facts.claim: Wintershall Dea's Russian holdings included a 35 percent interest in the Yuzhno-Russkoye field, 50 percent of two Siberian gas projects known collectively as Achimov, and a 15.5 percent position in the Nord Stream pipeline company and WIGA Transport Beteiligungs-GmbH & Co. KG.

sources.title: Nord Stream Partner to Withdraw from Russia

facts.claim: In December 2023 Harbour Energy agreed to acquire Wintershall Dea's upstream assets in Norway, Germany, Denmark, Argentina, Mexico, Egypt, Libya and Algeria, plus its European carbon capture and storage licences, at an enterprise value of $11.2 billion, excluding the Russian assets; BASF and LetterOne were to receive $2.15 billion in cash and new Harbour shares equal to 54.5 percent of the enlarged company, and Harbour assumed about $4.9 billion of Wintershall Dea bonds.

facts.claim: BASF announced on September 3, 2024 that the transfer of Wintershall Dea's E&P business to Harbour Energy had closed, all required approvals having been received earlier than initially expected; BASF's share of the consideration was $1.56 billion in cash and a 39.6 percent stake in Harbour.
